grammar.title: Future Time Clauses (when, as soon as, until)
grammar.explanation:
After **when**, **as soon as**, **until**, **before**, **after** and **once**, we use the **present simple**, not **will**, to talk about the future. We say 'I will call you **when** I get home', not 'when I will get home'.

The main clause uses **will** or an imperative. You can say 'Text me **when** you arrive'.

Use the **present perfect** to show the first action will be finished first. For example, 'I will go shopping **when** I have finished my work'.

**If** and **unless** work the same way. We say '**If** it rains, we will stay at home', not 'if it will rain'.

**When** means you are sure it will happen. **If** means it might happen.

Try it with today's words: 'I will pay with my credit card **when** I buy the next item'.
examples: *I'll send you the photos **when** I **get** home.* (when + present simple)
* **As soon as** the rain **stops**, we'll go for a walk.* (as soon as)
*Brush your teeth **before** you **go** to bed.* (imperative + before)
* **After** I **finish** university, I'm going to travel.* (after + going to)
*I'll call you **as soon as** I**'ve spoken** to the manager.* (present perfect: completion)

practice.q: Rewrite using 'as soon as': Sara will pay. First she will get cash from the cashpoint.
practice.a: Sara will pay as soon as she has got cash from the cashpoint.

practice.q: Rewrite using 'when': I will buy the furniture. First I will check my credit card.
practice.a: I will buy the furniture when I have checked my credit card.

practice.q: Rewrite using 'until': Do not pay for the item. First check the price.
practice.a: Do not pay for the item until you have checked the price.

practice.q: Rewrite using 'before': Put every item in your bag. Then leave the shop.
practice.a: Put every item in your bag before you leave the shop.
